# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

  <text x="40" y="85" font-family="Arial" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">17% Global Traffic Growth and Starlink's 3.3x Surge</text>
  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="40" y="100" width="1200" height="45" rx="4" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="127" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">Key Insight:</text>
  <text x="155" y="127" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">Global Internet traffic grew 17% YoY, with satellite connectivity (Starlink) surging 3.3x to reach underserved regions.</text>
  <!-- Left KPI card -->
  <rect x="40" y="165" width="380" height="200" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="200" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">GLOBAL TRAFFIC GROWTH</text>
  <text x="60" y="270" font-family="Arial" font-size="72" font-weight="bold" fill="#22C55E">17%</text>
  <text x="60" y="305" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">Year-over-Year Increase</text>
  <text x="60" y="330" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">vs. 2023 baseline</text>
  <!-- Right KPI card -->
  <rect x="440" y="165" width="380" height="200" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="460" y="200" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">STARLINK TRAFFIC GROWTH</text>
  <text x="460" y="270" font-family="Arial" font-size="72" font-weight="bold" fill="#F97316">3.3x</text>
  <text x="460" y="305" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">vs. Prior Year</text>
  <text x="460" y="330" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Satellite connectivity expansion</text>
  <!-- Starlink Image -->
  <rect x="840" y="165" width="400" height="200" rx="8" fill="#0F172A"/>
  <image href="../images/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg" x="850" y="175" width="380" height="180" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
  <!-- Bottom context -->
  <rect x="40" y="390" width="1200" height="120" rx="8" fill="#0F172A"/>
  <text x="60" y="420" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">Context</text>
  <text x="60" y="445" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">• Trend line normalized from mid-January to remove holiday volatility</text>
  <text x="60" y="468" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">• Starlink continued expansion to previously underserved geographic regions</text>
  <text x="60" y="491" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">• Increasing reliance on Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment & transportation</text>
  <!-- Data points -->
  <rect x="40" y="530" width="1200" height="100" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="560" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">ADDITIONAL METRICS</text>
  <text x="60" y="595" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">41%</text>
  <text x="140" y="595" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">of global traffic from mobile devices</text>
  <text x="480" y="595" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">28%</text>
  <text x="560" y="595" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">of dual-stack traffic on IPv6</text>
  <text x="900" y="595" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">33%</text>
  <text x="980" y="595" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">of traffic from iOS devices</text>
  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="680" x2="1240" y2="680" stroke="#1E3A5F" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="705" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#475569">Source: Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review | radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024</text>
  <text x="1240" y="705" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#475569">2</text>
</svg>

  <text x="40" y="85" font-family="Arial" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Post-Quantum Encryption Jumps from 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3</text>
  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="40" y="100" width="1200" height="45" rx="4" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="127" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">Key Insight:</text>
  <text x="155" y="127" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">Chrome 124's default post-quantum enablement (April 2024) drove dramatic adoption surge from ~2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic.</text>
  <!-- Three KPI cards row -->
  <!-- Card 1: Post-Quantum -->
  <rect x="40" y="160" width="380" height="180" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="190" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#94A3B8">POST-QUANTUM ENCRYPTION</text>
  <text x="60" y="235" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">TLS 1.3 Traffic</text>
  <text x="60" y="290" font-family="Arial" font-size="56" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">2%</text>
  <text x="120" y="290" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" fill="#22C55E">→ 13%</text>
  <text x="60" y="320" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">After Chrome 124 default (Apr 17, 2024)</text>
  <!-- Card 2: HTTP/3 -->
  <rect x="440" y="160" width="380" height="180" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="460" y="190" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#94A3B8">HTTP/3 ADOPTION</text>
  <text x="460" y="290" font-family="Arial" font-size="72" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">21%</text>
  <text x="460" y="320" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#94A3B8">of all traffic uses HTTP/3</text>
  <text x="460" y="340" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">QUIC-based, faster connections, encryption by default</text>
  <!-- Card 3: Go Language -->
  <rect x="840" y="160" width="400" height="180" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="860" y="190" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#94A3B8">TOP API CLIENT LANGUAGE</text>
  <text x="860" y="290" font-family="Arial" font-size="72" font-weight="bold" fill="#F97316">Go</text>
  <text x="980" y="290" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" fill="#94A3B8">~12%</text>
  <text x="860" y="320" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#94A3B8">of automated API requests</text>
  <text x="860" y="340" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">Surpassed Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%)</text>
  <!-- Bottom section: API Language breakdown -->
  <rect x="40" y="360" width="1200" height="130" rx="8" fill="#0F172A"/>
  <text x="60" y="390" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8" font-weight="bold">API CLIENT LANGUAGE BREAKDOWN</text>
  <!-- Language bars -->
  <g font-family="Arial">
    <text x="60" y="420" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="13">Go</text><rect x="140" y="408" width="180" height="16" rx="8" fill="#F97316"/><text x="330" y="422" fill="#94A3B8" font-size="12">~12%</text>
    <text x="400" y="420" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="13">Node.js</text><rect x="490" y="408" width="150" height="16" rx="8" fill="#2563EB"/>
    <text x="660" y="420" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="13">Python</text><rect x="750" y="408" width="144" height="16" rx="8" fill="#2563EB" opacity="0.8"/><text x="900" y="422" fill="#94A3B8" font-size="12">9.6%</text>
    <text x="400" y="450" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="13">Java</text><rect x="490" y="438" width="111" height="16" rx="8" fill="#2563EB" opacity="0.6"/><text x="610" y="450" fill="#94A3B8" font-size="12">7.4%</text>
    <text x="660" y="450" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="13">.NET</text><rect x="750" y="438" width="54" height="16" rx="8" fill="#2563EB" opacity="0.4"/><text x="810" y="450" fill="#94A3B8" font-size="12">3.6%</text>
  </g>
  <!-- Browser share -->
  <rect x="40" y="510" width="580" height="100" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="540" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8" font-weight="bold">BROWSER MARKET SHARE</text>
  <text x="60" y="575" font-family="Arial" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Chrome</text>
  <text x="170" y="575" font-family="Arial" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563EB">Dominant</text>
  <text x="60" y="600" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Global browser market leadership continues</text>
  <!-- Mobile OS -->
  <rect x="640" y="510" width="600" height="100" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="660" y="540" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8" font-weight="bold">MOBILE OS LANDSCAPE</text>
  <text x="660" y="575" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Android peak: 95%+</text>
  <text x="900" y="575" font-family="Arial" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">iOS share: 33%</text>
  <text x="660" y="600" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Regional variations significant; iOS peaks at ~66% in some markets</text>
  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="680" x2="1240" y2="680" stroke="#1E3A5F" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="705" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#475569">Source: Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review | Post-quantum: Chrome 124 enabled default Apr 17, 2024</text>
  <text x="1240" y="705" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#475569">4</text>
</svg>

  <text x="40" y="85" font-family="Arial" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Five Takeaways Shaping the 2025 Internet Outlook</text>
  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="40" y="100" width="1200" height="45" rx="4" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <text x="60" y="127" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">Summary:</text>
  <text x="130" y="127" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#94A3B8">Key findings from 2024 that inform strategic planning for network and security leaders.</text>
  <!-- Five takeaways in cards -->
  <!-- Takeaway 1 -->
  <rect x="40" y="160" width="720" height="90" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <circle cx="70" cy="205" r="20" fill="#2563EB"/>
  <text x="70" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">1</text>
  <text x="105" y="195" font-family="Arial" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Traffic Growth Trajectory</text>
  <text x="105" y="220" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">17% YoY global traffic growth sustained — driven by expanding connectivity, commerce, and digital services.</text>
  <!-- Takeaway 2 -->
  <rect x="780" y="160" width="460" height="90" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <circle cx="810" cy="205" r="20" fill="#22C55E"/>

  <text x="845" y="195" font-family="Arial" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Post-Quantum Momentum</text>
  <text x="845" y="220" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">13% adoption and climbing — Chrome 124 default driving rapid encryption upgrades.</text>
  <!-- Takeaway 3 -->
  <rect x="40" y="265" width="720" height="90" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <circle cx="70" cy="310" r="20" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="70" y="317" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">3</text>
  <text x="105" y="300" font-family="Arial" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Connectivity Fragility</text>
  <text x="105" y="325" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">Government shutdowns = #1 disruption cause (116+ incidents). Digital infrastructure is a policy target.</text>
  <!-- Takeaway 4 -->
  <rect x="780" y="265" width="460" height="90" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <circle cx="810" cy="310" r="20" fill="#F97316"/>
  <text x="810" y="317" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">4</text>
  <text x="845" y="300" font-family="Arial" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Persistent Security Threats</text>
  <text x="845" y="325" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">6.5% traffic mitigated; Log4j exploitation continues 2+ years post-disclosure.</text>
  <!-- Takeaway 5 -->
  <rect x="40" y="370" width="1200" height="90" rx="8" fill="#1A3A5C"/>
  <circle cx="70" cy="415" r="20" fill="#9C27B0"/>
  <text x="70" y="422" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">5</text>
  <text x="105" y="405" font-family="Arial" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Evolving Developer Ecosystem</text>
  <text x="105" y="430" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8">Go surpasses Node.js and Python to become the #1 API client language (~12% of automated traffic).</text>
  <!-- Bottom section: 2025 Outlook -->
  <rect x="40" y="480" width="1200" height="130" rx="8" fill="#0F172A"/>
  <text x="60" y="510" font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#94A3B8" font-weight="bold">2025 OUTLOOK INDICATORS</text>
  <g font-family="Arial">
    <text x="60" y="545" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#22C55E">↑</text>
    <text x="90" y="545" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF">Traffic growth to continue as connectivity expands</text>
    <text x="60" y="575" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563EB">↑</text>
    <text x="90" y="575" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF">Post-quantum encryption adoption accelerating</text>
    <text x="60" y="605" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">⚠</text>
    <text x="90" y="605" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF">Internet shutdowns and disruptions likely to persist as policy tool</text>
    <text x="540" y="545" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#F97316">↑</text>
    <text x="570" y="545" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF">AI services continuing meteoric rise</text>
    <text x="540" y="575" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#9C27B0">↑</text>
    <text x="570" y="575" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF">Go and modern languages gaining API share</text>
    <text x="540" y="605" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">⚠</text>
    <text x="570" y="605" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF">Legacy vulnerabilities (Log4j) remain exploitable</text>
  </g>

  <line x1="40" y1="680" x2="1240" y2="680" stroke="#1E3A5F" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="705" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#475569">Source: Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review | Strategic planning guidance for 2025</text>
  <text x="1240" y="705" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#475569">7</text>
</svg>

# 01_title

Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review — Opening slide.

This report presents the most significant Internet trends from 2024, including traffic growth, technology adoption shifts, connectivity challenges, and the evolving security landscape.

Data is derived from Cloudflare's global network, which protects and accelerates websites and applications for millions of customers worldwide. The analysis covers January through December 2024.

Key points: (1) Comprehensive view of Internet patterns and trends (2) Data from Cloudflare's global network position (3) Informs strategic planning for network and security leaders

Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_traffic_growth

[Transition] Let's begin with the headline finding: global Internet traffic grew substantially in 2024.

Global Internet traffic grew 17% year-over-year in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. [Pause]

The most remarkable growth story is Starlink. SpaceX's satellite Internet service saw a dramatic 3.3x surge during 2024, continuing to bring connectivity to previously underserved locations. [Data] 3.3x — that's more than triple the prior year. [Benchmark] This growth rate far exceeds the overall Internet traffic growth of 17%. [Pause]

Additional context: 41% of global traffic came from mobile devices, reflecting the continued importance of mobile connectivity worldwide. IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic.

Key points: (1) 17% YoY global traffic growth sustained (2) Starlink surged 3.3x — satellite connectivity expanding (3) Mobile (41%) and IPv6 (28%) continue upward trajectory

Duration: 3 minutes

Flex: [If time is tight, skip mobile/IPv6 details and focus on 17% and Starlink 3.3x]

---

# 03_top_services

[Transition] Building on traffic growth, let's examine which services drove the most Internet activity.

Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. [Pause]

The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver. Google leads at #1, followed by Facebook (#2), Apple (#3), TikTok (#4), AWS (#5), Microsoft (#6), Instagram (#7), YouTube (#8), Amazon (#9), and WhatsApp (#10). [Data] Google commands 89% of search engine referral traffic. [Benchmark] This dominance in both top service ranking and search is a powerful combination.

A significant trend to note: Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. AI services are disrupting traditional service rankings in real-time. [Pause]

Key points: (1) Google #1 for second consecutive year (2) Generative AI meteoric rise reshaping rankings (3) Metaverse receded; AI the defining trend of 2024

Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 04_technology_adoption

[Transition] Turning to technology adoption — the numbers here tell a compelling story about the speed of modern encryption upgrades.

Post-quantum encryption saw a dramatic surge in adoption during 2024. Starting at around 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17, rapidly climbing to approximately 12-13%. [Data] 2% to 13% — that's a 6.5x increase in just months. [Benchmark] This is one of the fastest technology adoption curves we've observed. Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing. [Pause]

HTTP/3 reached 21% adoption — the most recent version of the protocol running on QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.

Perhaps most remarkably in the developer ecosystem: Go is now the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, surpassing Node.js and Python (9.6%). [Data] Go at 12% leads all languages for API automation. [Pause]

Key points: (1) Post-quantum: 2% → 13% after Chrome 124 default (2) HTTP/3 at 21% adoption (3) Go #1 API language, capturing ~12% of automated traffic

Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_disruptions

[Transition] Connectivity is not just about growth — there are significant fragility points to acknowledge.

Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. These outages result from a variety of causes, and the Cloudflare Radar Outage Center tracks their scope and duration. [Pause]

The leading cause: Government-directed shutdowns at 116+ incidents. [Data] More than half of all major disruptions were deliberate government actions. [Benchmark] This is nearly 3x the next closest cause. [Scan Room] This has significant implications for organizations with global operations.

Following government shutdowns: Cable cuts (41 incidents), power outages (16), technical problems (9), military action (9), and weather (8). [Pause]

The strategic implication is clear: organizations must plan for Internet connectivity fragility as a persistent reality, not an anomaly. Government-directed shutdowns are now a regular feature of the global Internet landscape.

Key points: (1) 225 major disruptions observed in 2024 (2) Government shutdowns = #1 cause at 116+ incidents (3) Cable cuts (41) and power outages (16) follow — connectivity fragility is a strategic risk

Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 06_security

[Transition] Now to security — and the findings here demand attention.

Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed, indicating the scale of ongoing threats. [Data] 6.5% — that's a substantial percentage of all Internet traffic being malicious or requiring mitigation. [Pause]

The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries. [Benchmark] Bot concentration is extremely high — a small number of countries are the primary source of automated threat traffic.

Perhaps most concerning: The Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later. [Data] Log4j still being actively exploited 2+ years post-disclosure. [Pause] This underscores the persistent nature of widely known vulnerabilities.

In email security: 4.3% of emails processed were malicious, with 43% containing deceptive links. The top-level domain .bar originated the largest share of malicious and spam email.

RPKI valid routes increased by 6.4% — a positive step toward improved Internet routing security.

Key points: (1) 6.5% traffic mitigation rate — threats at scale (2) Log4j still exploited 2+ years post-disclosure (3) Gambling/Games most attacked; 68% bot traffic from top 10 countries

Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five strategic takeaways that should shape your 2025 planning.

First, Traffic Growth Trajectory: The 17% year-over-year growth in global Internet traffic shows no signs of slowing. Connectivity expansion, digital commerce, and online services continue to drive sustained demand. Plan for continued growth.

Second, Post-Quantum Momentum: The rapid adoption of post-quantum encryption — from 2% to 13% following Chrome 124's default — signals a fast-moving transition. Organizations not yet on this path need to accelerate planning.

Third, Connectivity Fragility: Government-directed shutdowns remain the leading cause of major Internet disruptions. This is a policy and geopolitical reality that creates operational risk for global businesses.

Fourth, Persistent Security Threats: 6.5% traffic mitigation, ongoing Log4j exploitation, and bot concentration demonstrate that security threats are not theoretical — they are ongoing and persistent.

Fifth, Evolving Developer Ecosystem: Go surpassing Node.js and Python to become the #1 API client language reflects shifting technology preferences that will affect procurement, integration, and hiring decisions.

[Scan Room] These five themes — growth, encryption, fragility, threats, and ecosystem shifts — together define the Internet landscape as we enter 2025.

Key points: (1) 17% traffic growth sustained (2) Post-quantum at 13% and climbing (3) Government shutdowns = #1 disruption risk (4) 6.5% mitigated; Log4j persists (5) Go leads API client languages

Duration: 3 minutes

Flex: [If time is tight, focus on takeaways 1, 3, and 4 as the most strategically critical]
